newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's Vilnius optimistic on profit. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's Vilnius optimistic on profit. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects name throughout from Raimondas Kutras to Raimondas Kutra)
Vilnius Bank said on Friday it expected profits this year to be sharply higher at 20 million litas versus the 2.9 million litas of 1995.
The bank is Lithuania's leading financial institution and has Western firms as well as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) as major shareholders.
"We are expecting a profit of 20 million litas for 1996," Vilnius Bank deputy chairman Raimondas Kutra told Reuters in an interview.
The bank made a profit of 16 million litas in the first nine months of the year and its assets rose to 788.8 million litas from 408.4 million litas in the same period.
It has weathered well the banking crisis which hit Lithuania at the end of last year.
It has a quote on the Vilnius bourse and recently became the first Baltic bank to release global depository receipts (GDRs) which are quoted in Luxembourg.
"Our results have been good and this has been reflected in the performance of our shares and our GDRs," Kutra added.
The bank recently split its shares from a nominal 500 litas to 50 litas. The shares currently trade at around 140 litas.
"We do not have any plans for a new GDR issue, we must work with our new share capital and make a return on investment," Kutra added.
"Instead, we may look at the possibility of securing a subordinated or syndicated loan," he added.
Kutra said that unlike Estonia's largest bank Hansapank it had no plans to expand to the neighbouring Baltic states.
"The markets in Latvia and Estonia are quite crowded, it is not the right time to compete in other Baltic banking markets," Kutra said.
Kutra said that the bank was exploring the idea of buying into another bank but would not name any names.
Hansapank earlier this year bought Latvia's Deutsche-Lettische Bank and renamed it Hansabank Latvija.
This was the first cross-border merger in the Baltic market but sector consolidation is expected in all three countries.
Kutra said his bank's focus was on serving customers in the local corporate market and unlike some other banks it did not depend too heavily on the domestic T-bill market for revenue.
The bank's loan portfolio is currently worth 448.5 million litas and it has only 46.5 million litas of government T-bills on its books.
